findings: Source review identified the legitimate mark state closed through the existing denied helper; the new adapter preserves it as a terminal observation, not permission to create.

Initial primary adapter tests reproduced evaluation of a rejected observation getter by an outer Zod refinement. A transform after successful parsing fixed this new-adapter defect; the accessor regression passed. A deliberately invalid-client fixture cast was also corrected for strict TypeScript.

The first SQL run's expired-proof fixture correctly hit the existing proof CHECK because only expires_ms changed. Correcting both verified_ms and expires_ms produced an internally valid expired fixture; no constraint was weakened and no existing SQL was changed.

Marked is offline observation only. Existing base inspect consumes its own proof; trusted fresh-proof coordinator for mark remains absent.
Provider finality/authenticated evidence verifier, real Auth/session provisioning/revocation propagation and production host remain absent.

next: Implement an inactive trusted coordinator that obtains a fresh INSPECT proof and records one capacity marker for an already admitted claim, without first consuming that receipt in base inspect.
